notes:
CRM notes: heavy emphasis on deterministic throughput and unit economics. Meridian runs user-personalization + ad-rerank pipeline: mix of chat endpoints (low-latency interactive) and embedding bulk jobs overnight. Key quote on 2026-02-04 call: 'We need predictable per-token cost for billing our customers — can't have wild swings.'

Cost model specifics discussed: commit tiers (16 / 24 / 40 GPU-equivalents), assumed avg util 60% steady-state, peak util 85% with burst to shared pool. We modeled batching factor 3-5 depending on latency SLO; effective tokens/sec per A100-eq ~ 800–1,100 for chat (with batching) and ~2,500 for embeddings. Prefix/KV cache apply: expected 20-25% cache hit reduces served tokens by ~15% effective.

Unit economics snapshot (internal):
- 24-reserved baseline -> list price $X/month (confidential in drive). Amortized infra + support -> effective $0.22 - $0.35 per 1k tokens under 60% util assumptions.
- If util drops to 40% cost per 1k tokens jumps ~1.6x -> major blocker for their finance team.
- Fallback routing to hosted (for burst) assumed at ~1.4x unit price; they want explicit burn-down window and billing caps.

SLA/contract items: Meridian requires p95 < 120ms (chat) and p99 < 450ms. Proposed SLA credit: tiered up to 10% of monthly invoice for sustained degradations; Meridian legal pushing to 20% and tighter measurement windows. They want explicit maintenance windows (not counted as SLA violations) and a defined rolling 30-day measurement for credits.

Security/compliance: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS mandatory. On-prem appliance possible but timelines: 8-12 weeks for air-gapped validation. Data residency: must keep EU user data in eu-1 region where applicable.

Next steps from AE/SE: update cost model with 6-month pilot commit (recalculate per-token under expected 65% util), include burst pricing annex, and provide redlined SLA template for their counsel.
cost_model_highlights: Commit tiers evaluated: 16 / 24 / 40 GPU-eq reserved; each tier has different amortization of infra/support costs
Utilization assumptions: base-case 60% avg, optimistic 75%, pessimistic 40% — permutations drive per-token variance 1.0x / 0.82x / 1.6x
Batching assumptions: interactive chat batching 2-4; embeddings batch 16-64 — batching reduces per-token GPU cycles by ~25-45% depending on model
Cache assumptions: KV/prefix cache hit 20-25% -> effective token load down ~15%
Effective tokens/sec per A100-eq: chat 800-1,100 (batched), embeddings 2,000-2,800
Fallback economics: hosted fallback priced at 1.3-1.6x dedicated per-token; contract should specify monthly cap on fallback spend
SLA economics: propose credit cap 10% monthly invoice; Meridian pushing for 15-20% — negotiation point
Break-even horizon: 6-9 months for 24-GPU-eq commit vs pure hosted at their forecasted volume (assumes 65% util)
deployment_notes: Network: VPC peering + dedicated peering, 1-10 Gbps links for low-latency traffic. On-prem option requires ops window and signed HLD. KMS: integrate customer-managed keys; retention controls required for EU data. Non-prod telemetry allowed to cross-cloud if pseudonymized.
